title: Altaira Commerce — Inference fit and toolchain scouting
summary: Intro discovery for model selection and deployment mode — customer has mixed multi‑language search and assistant workloads, strong data residency requirements, wants tool‑calling and long context. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs and next steps for a short POC and security pack.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-24 16:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Carlos Mendes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Altaira Head of AI), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Mei Chen (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to understand inference fit for Altaira's commerce assistant and product search. Need high context for multi-turn product threads, multilingual support (EN/ES/PT/FR), and callable tools (inventory lookup, pricing API). Evaluated Hosted for fast start, Dedicated for predictable latency/cost, Private for data residency. Action items and POC plan agreed.

00:00 Carlos: hey everyone thanks for joining uh we'll wait another 30 seconds then kick off.
00:22 Lena: no problem, thanks Carlos. we have about an hour set aside.
00:35 Carlos: great — quick round robin introductions? i'm carlos, account exec, and priya here is our SE, she'll run through technical bits.
00:44 Priya: hi all, priya nair, solution engineer focused on inference and runtime — happy to dig into latency and tooling.
00:52 Lena: lena ortiz, head of ai at altaira. we run the product search and customer assistant teams.
00:57 Samir: samir patel, platform eng, i manage k8s infra and data residency controls.
01:02 Mei: mei chen, product manager for our assistant experience.
01:10 Carlos: awesome. high level — what's top priority: quality vs latency vs cost?
01:22 Lena: quality first for the assistant — we need it to keep context across long support threads, sometimes 8–10 messages and product catalogs appended. latency is second but we want under 600ms for web chat ideally. cost matters as volume is high.
01:38 Priya: okay that's helpful. when you say long context, are you thinking 16k, 32k, or more? what's your longest prompt+history now?
01:47 Lena: average is about 4–6k tokens but peak sessions go to 30k when we include product descriptions, images metadata, and past conversation.
01:56 Priya: got it — so we should look at models with 32k+ context or solutions that support segmented retrieval + KV cache.
02:06 Samir: quick note on security — we have EU data residency requirements, SOC2 plus internal audit logs and KMS for key management. we need SSO (SAML) too.
02:17 Carlos: understood — Redwood supports hosted api, dedicated pools, and private VPC/on-prem. for KMS we integrate with customer KMS in private deployments; for hosted we have envelope encryption and SOC2 compliance.
02:30 Mei: are there feature differences between hosted and dedicated for tooling? we rely on tool-calling for inventory lookups (real time) and a pricing microservice.
02:40 Priya: function/tool calling is supported across modes, but dedicated gives you more throughput headroom and predictable tail latency for synchronous calls. hosted is easiest to get started and supports streaming and function calling, but if you need hard SLOs at peak, dedicated or private is safer.
03:05 Lena: pricing wise, do you have ballpark numbers for 32k context models?
03:13 Carlos: i'll send formal pricing, but quickguides — hosted is usage-based per token, dedicated is committed monthly capacity which reduces unit cost for high throughput. private has licensing plus infra. i'll share a spreadsheet after.
03:32 Samir: any limits on tool calls per second in hosted? we might do a fan‑out to 3 services for a single user action.
03:42 Priya: hosted has burst policies and rate limits; we can configure async patterns for fan-out. dedicated lets you reserve concurrency and route by policy so you don't hit noisy neighbor issues.
03:55 Mei: on multilingual — we support EN/ES/FR/PT and some local dialects. do you recommend a single multi‑lingual model or language-specific models?
04:07 Priya: depends — a single large multilingual model (eg Mistral-like or Llama derivatives) simplifies ops but can be heavier. language-specific smaller models can be more cost efficient and sometimes better quality. Redwood Console helps route requests to tuned variants by region/language.
04:27 Lena: we have some internal translation post-processing — might be fine with a single model as long as it handles idiomatic phrases.
04:35 Carlos: any regulatory constraints for hosting in EU vs US?
04:41 Samir: EU data must remain in EU for certain customers; also need audit logs retained for 7 years.
04:49 Priya: private deployment supports customer-managed regions and audit retention. hosted can be region pinned to EU cloud region and we can extend logs, but there are limits; we'll capture exact SLAs in the security pack.
05:05 Lena: about hallucinations — we need strong ground-truth retrieval and tool calling to reduce hallucination risk. we also need deterministic rerank for search results.
05:17 Priya: Redwood Optimize suggests caching and reranker setups and provides eval hooks to monitor regression on prompt sets. for retrieval you can plug your vector database and use retrieval augmentation; tool‑calling ensures access to live inventory for factual answers.
05:36 Mei: curious about latency budgets: 600ms for chat, search can tolerate up to 1s. how do you manage batching without blowing chat latency?
05:47 Priya: continuous batching and dynamic thresholds — for chat we favor low-latency paths and smaller batches; for high-throughput queries we allow larger batch windows. you can set per-route policies in Redwood Console.
06:05 Carlos: are there any legal or procurement timelines we should know about?
06:11 Lena: procurement sequence typically takes 6–8 weeks; legal wants SOC2 and encryption details. decision target for pilot is end of Q1.
06:20 Carlos: good. quick technical dive — priya can you walk through a 32k context test configuration?
06:26 Priya: sure. so we'd pick a model variant that supports 32k context (there are open models with extensions) or use segment+kv cache to stitch context. in Dedicated, we can allocate GPU pools tuned for long context with modified attention kernels. in hosted we surface verified model profiles and memory‑optimized routing.
06:48 Samir: when you say 'verified model profiles' — what does that include?
06:52 Priya: per-model perf bench marks: tokens/sec, cold-start latency, GPU memory footprint, and sample output quality metrics on common prompt suites. sometimes names are transcribed oddly in our internal docs, sorry, but we'll share the verified bench doc.
07:08 Mei: can we run a small latency POC where we call the pricing API as a tool and measure end-to-end tail latency?
07:15 Carlos: yes — typical POC includes a small throughput test (1–5 qps), functional testing for tool calling, and an eval harness across prompt sets.
07:24 Lena: what about model updates and rollbacks? we need canary and A/B testing.
07:29 Priya: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies if a new variant regresses. Console shows per-route metrics and model-level regressions tied to eval prompt sets.
07:45 Samir: networking for private — do you support on-prem via air‑gapped install or only VPC?
07:50 Priya: both. Private supports VPC peering and on-prem packages for air‑gapped setups; there are additional ops requirements for on‑prem.
07:59 Lena: any specifics on KMS? we use HashiCorp Vault currently.
08:04 Priya: we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for Vault we can support envelope encryption patterns with your keys in Vault. we'll need an architecture call to scope secrets flow.
08:20 Mei: can you summarize tradeoffs if we start hosted then move to dedicated/private later?
08:26 Carlos: common path: start hosted to validate product, then move to dedicated for predictable unit economics as traffic grows, and then private for strict residency/regulatory demands. Redwood makes model and rollout configs portable across modes.
08:43 Lena: that migration path sounds good. any gotchas?
08:47 Priya: data egress and keys are the typical friction points. also model variants and quantization may differ between on‑prem hardware; we'll plan an onboarding test to validate parity.
09:02 Samir: curious about quantization — do you recommend int8 or more aggressive for long context models?
09:09 Priya: int8 often gives a good balance, some workloads can tolerate int4 but it's model dependent. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization for your workload and profile tradeoffs.
09:24 Mei: for POC success criteria, we propose: 1) max 600ms median chat latency, 2) end-to-end tool calls under 250ms, 3) consistent multilingual quality on 5 prompt sets.
09:36 Carlos: that seems reasonable. we'll map that to POC tests.
09:41 Lena: procurement will ask for compliance artifacts — can you share SOC2 report and data flow diagram?
09:47 Carlos: yes, we'll include SOC2, ISO if available, and a data flow diagram in the security pack.
09:54 Priya: also to note — for multilingual tokenization we sometimes see tokenization blowups on languages with different alphabets; we'll run a token analysis on your QA data set.
10:09 Samir: do you have an integration example for a pricing endpoint with tool-calling?
10:13 Priya: yes we have example flows and a quickstart repo — i'll share a sample that demonstrates function signatures, streaming responses, and error handling patterns.
10:25 Mei: regarding cost, can you give an estimate if we expect 50k messages/day with average 6k tokens? rough ballpark fine.
10:34 Carlos: i'll compute a preliminary estimate in the pricing spreadsheet — that'll show hosted per-token vs projected dedicated unit cost for commit tiers.
10:45 Lena: any concerns with stateful memory for long conversations? we do a hybrid of vector store plus KV cache.
10:51 Priya: that hybrid is common — use retrieval to compress long histories into salient facts and kv cache for fast recent tokens. Redwood runtime supports client-managed vs server-managed KV caches.
11:05 Samir: do you expose metrics for token counts per request and per-route cost breakdown?
11:11 Priya: yes Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model. you can also get traces for individual requests.
11:23 Mei: timeline — we'd like to kick off a 4-week POC in January. legal needs docs before end of year.
11:31 Carlos: noted. we'll target security pack by next week and pricing + POC plan by end of month.
11:39 Lena: cool. any final technical questions?
11:44 Samir: one more — fallback behavior if primary model overloads.
11:48 Priya: we recommend fallback to smaller quantized variants or region failover. Redwood routing can automatically fallback by policy.
11:58 Carlos: ok let's capture action items and next steps. thanks everyone.
12:05 Lena: thanks all, bye.
12:08 Mei: thanks.

End transcript.
next_steps: Send security pack (SOC2, data flow, KMS integration notes)
Share pricing spreadsheet with hosted vs dedicated vs private estimates
Schedule POC kickoff planning call (target Jan)
action_items: Carlos Mendes - Send dedicated vs hosted pricing + reference benchmarks - 2026-11-27
Priya Nair - Share sample tool-calling quickstart repo and example for pricing API - 2026-11-26
Priya Nair - Run tokenization analysis on provided multilingual sample dataset - 2026-11-30
Lena Ortiz - Provide sample prompt sets and list of top 100 SKU docs for POC - 2026-11-29
